title: Reliance on cloud provider data centers and shared responsibility
status_rationale: Unbound requirements specify one managed PostgreSQL cluster with per-sponsor schemas (CNV-ARC-001) and per-tenant backup honoring boundaries (UNB-TEN-014), implying a managed cloud provider, but no provider, region or deployment exists.
target_answer: Echelon operates no data centers or server rooms. Customer data is hosted with a major cloud provider in United States regions, including backups and disaster recovery copies, enforced by infrastructure-as-code region pinning and an organization policy that denies resource creation elsewhere. Production spans multiple availability zones, with a documented regional recovery approach. Physical and environmental controls are inherited from the provider and evidenced by its SOC 2 Type II and ISO/IEC 27001 reports, which we review annually, mapping provider complementary user entity controls to our own controls. We publish the shared responsibility split.
current_practice: No production hosting selected or deployed.
intended_practice: Select provider and regions as part of Unbound deployment architecture.
customer_statement: Echelon does not operate data centers. Production hosting has not yet been selected; we plan to use a major cloud provider's US regions and rely on its independently audited physical controls.

challenge.customer_intent: Data is physically protected and available.
challenge.adverse_outcome: Physical intrusion, environmental failure or regional outage affects data.
challenge.conventional_control_effectiveness: Questionnaire items about badge readers, CCTV and generators are irrelevant to a cloud-hosted vendor except through the provider's report.
challenge.contractually_required: Physical security sections appear in most questionnaires.
challenge.historical_convention: Site inspections and physical security attestations.
challenge.architectural_elimination: No vendor-operated facility holds customer data, eliminating vendor facility risk within that scope.
challenge.automatic_enforcement: Region pinning policy and IaC drift detection.
challenge.stronger_alternative: Inherit and verify provider assurance; answer physical items as not applicable with evidence.
challenge.alternative_verifiable: Yes, via provider reports and configuration evidence.
challenge.invalidating_conditions: Customer data on endpoints or local servers.
supporting_arguments: Major providers' audited controls exceed what a small vendor could build.
opposing_arguments: Provider reports carve out customer-configured controls; misconfiguration is the vendor's responsibility.

title: Offices, physical records and on-premises processing
status_rationale: The principal office is TODO in the formation values file. Whether Echelon has any office is not established.
target_answer: Echelon has no office that stores or processes customer data; any office or coworking space is used for work on company-managed devices only. No customer data is stored on local servers. Paper records with customer information are not created; if received, they are digitized to the controlled system and cross-cut shredded, with the disposal recorded.
customer_statement: Echelon does not plan to store or process customer data at any office location. Office arrangements are not yet established.

title: Remote work security
status_rationale: Echelon appears to be a remote, distributed operation, but no remote work policy was located.
target_answer: All work is remote by design. Customer data is accessed only inside managed cloud environments through phishing-resistant authentication from company-managed devices; it is not stored on endpoints. Remote workers follow a remote work standard covering private workspace, screen privacy, home network hygiene and use of trusted networks or the company VPN or zero-trust access path. Access from outside approved jurisdictions is blocked by conditional access.
intended_practice: Adopt remote work standard and conditional access.
customer_statement: A remote work security standard is planned. Customer data is intended to remain in managed cloud environments rather than on personnel devices.

title: Endpoints, authenticators and media sanitization
status_rationale: No device inventory, management or disposal records were located.
target_answer: Only company-managed endpoints with full-disk encryption, automatic updates, screen lock, endpoint protection and remote wipe may access company systems, enforced by device posture checks at sign-in; personal devices are not permitted for administrative or customer-data access. Lost or stolen devices are reported within 24 hours and wiped. Administrative accounts require hardware-backed phishing-resistant authenticators, with registered backup authenticators held separately so loss of one key does not lock out or force weaker recovery. Retired devices and media are sanitized per NIST SP 800-88 with a certificate.
intended_practice: Adopt device management and authenticator standard.
customer_statement: Managed endpoint, authenticator and media sanitization standards are planned and not yet evidenced.

title: Physical concentration risk of a small, co-located team
status_rationale: Personnel location and number are not established; business continuity requirements (UNB-GAP-028) exist only as design.
target_answer: We document where personnel are located and plan for a regional event that disables all of them: at least two people able to perform critical operations from different regions or a contracted backup operator, no critical operation that depends on a single physical device or location (backup authenticators and credential custody held separately), and the ability to operate from any managed device with internet access. Any equipment we operate ourselves has power, fire and flood protection appropriate to its role, though the target is to operate none. We explain to customers that a site inspection adds little for a cloud-hosted service and offer provider reports and configuration evidence instead, while permitting an inspection on request.
intended_practice: Document locations and backup operator arrangements in continuity plan.
customer_statement: Physical concentration and single-device dependencies have not yet been assessed. Mitigations through backup operators and separated credential custody are planned.

challenge.customer_intent: A local disaster at the vendor does not stop the service.
challenge.adverse_outcome: Storm, power or connectivity loss in one area disables everyone able to operate the service.
challenge.conventional_control_effectiveness: Conventional physical controls (generators, alternate offices) target facilities, not the real dependency of a remote micro-team on people and personal devices.
challenge.contractually_required: Business continuity clauses commonly require recovery capability.
challenge.historical_convention: Alternate work sites and site inspections.
challenge.architectural_elimination: Cloud-hosted, device-independent operation removes facility dependency.
challenge.stronger_alternative: Geographically separated operators and separated credential custody.
challenge.customer_acceptance_likelihood: Likely if a backup operator exists; uncertain otherwise.
challenge.invalidating_conditions: All operators and custodians in one region.
challenge.alternative_risks: Backup operator is another third party with access.
supporting_arguments: Targets the actual single points of failure.
opposing_arguments: A backup operator may not be able to act quickly without prior hands-on experience.
